Theme 056 · Signature directions

Workflow Canvas

The film lives on a dark, dot-gridded automation canvas: nodes, bezier cables, glowing packets that hop one node per beat and status rings (grey idle · teal running · green done · coral exception). Teal carries the flow; coral is reserved for the single exception branch that needs a human — which makes the agent look auditable, not magical.

readability ●●○trust ●●●effort med
1 · HOOK0:00–0:08

Nodes pop in from the corners every two beats, then red dashed cables draw across each other and fall loose with × ends; on bar 3’s downbeat every status ring flips to coral “!” at once and the cables shiver.

2 · REVEAL0:08 (drop)

On the drop the red tangle snaps straight — all cables turn teal in one frame and route into a single port; packets race to the hub, it flashes white, the wordmark unmasks and the coral “You decide” node plugs into the bottom port on the sting.

3 · PROOF MOMENT0:12–0:32

The camera dives into the pipeline; packets hop Deploy → Checkout → Metrics one node per beat while a dashed audit link wakes Pulse below; on the bar-9 downbeat Checkout’s ring turns coral and one packet peels off down the coral branch to the exception card and the Roll back node.

4 · CTA0:36–0:45

The camera pulls back until the flow is a minimap; the hub grows at centre, the tagline sets, and on the sting downbeat the coral Start free node drops in and a packet travels the cable into it.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Dot-grid canvas — deep navy with a 36 px dot grid; the camera only pans and zooms, never cuts inside a scene
  • Node + ports — r28 square, glyph, label below, in/out ports; max 7 nodes per frame
  • Status ring — grey idle · teal running · green done · coral exception — the whole story in four colours
  • Bezier cable + packet — glowing dot with a soft halo that hops one node per beat
  • Audit link — dashed teal cable: Pulse observes the pipeline without sitting in it
  • Exception branch — the only coral cable in the film, ending in a human decision node

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Packet hop — packet travels one cable per beat (0.5 s at 120 BPM), power1.inOut, with a 0.15 s ring pulse on arrival
  • Cable snap — dashed red → solid teal in a single frame on the drop, then path-morph to straight over 0.3 s expo.out
  • Canvas camera — pan/zoom only: 1 bar zoom-in (expo.inOut 2 s) into the node that matters; pull-back to minimap for the CTA

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Engineers and ops buyers already think in pipelines, and a canvas shows exactly where the agent sits and where the human stays in control. Risk: spaghetti — more than seven nodes or more than one coral branch and the frame becomes a diagram nobody reads.

Adapt to your product: Draw your customer’s real process as 4–6 nodes, place your product as a node or an audit link, and give the single exception path its own colour ending in a human action.

References: https://docs.n8n.io/courses/level-one/chapter-1/ (node-canvas editor conventions (ports, nodes, execution state)) · https://docs.n8n.io/build/understand-workflows/workflow-components/canvas-groups (grouping nodes on a canvas)
